channel.title: Spotlight Delaware – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Spotlight Delaware – Bias and Credibility (spotlightdelaware.org)

item.title: Get Involved: Data center appeal, opioid settlement funds, budgets unveiled, more
item.description: A rundown of some of the most important or interesting public meetings happening around Delaware this week.

item.title: Democrats want to boost solar power through two bills in the General Assembly
item.description: Delaware lawmakers advanced two bills last week that would remove regulatory obstacles facing solar projects, just as the state scrambles to increase energy production amid soaring electricity prices.

item.title: Carney calls for a $20M housing fund in next Wilmington budget
item.description: Wilmington Mayor John Carney introduced his city budget Thursday and within it was a proposal to create a $20 million program to incentivize the construction of new housing.

item.title: Delaware approves $475K in opioid grants for local governments
item.description: The Delaware Prescription Opioid Settlement Distribution Commission approved three grants on Monday for Seaford, Wilmington and Newark.

item.title: Delaware proposes regulations on crypto, with licensing for stablecoins
item.description: With two bills introduced Monday, Delaware could become one of the first states to regulate the use of stablecoins in finance.

item.title: Meyer removes longtime budget official following critical comments
item.description: Gov. Matt Meyer fired a longtime Delaware budget forecaster on Wednesday, a day after a report that he criticized the Meyer administration over transparency surrounding the state's prominent corporate franchise.

item.title: Delaware City data center environmental denial upheld by state board
item.description: A Delaware board upheld a decision that the Project Washington data center is not allowed under the Coastal Zone Act.

item.title: From employee to owner: How an immigrant-owned café is attracting more Latinos
item.description: Miriam Molina Mendez wants to welcome more customers from Latino and immigrant communities into her Delaware Art Museum-based coffee shop.

item.title: Get Involved: Corner store bans, affordable housing changes, more
item.description: Wilmington votes on political party switches and corner stores , and Sussex County affordable housing, lead this week's public meetings.

item.title: 'Beyond the Headlines' podcast: On the waves with Leipsic watermen
item.description: Deputy editor Tim Carlin is the guest for this episode of “Beyond the Headlines,” to discuss reporting on Leipsic watermen.

item.title: Delaware court ruling marks a victory for Maryland offshore wind project
item.description: The Baltimore company behind plans to build a wind farm off the Ocean City, Maryland coastline scored a victory last week when a Delaware judge upheld a law stripping Sussex County of its ability to deny a substation permit for the renewable energy project.

item.title: Dover shelter’s future in question as city challenges zoning
item.description: The city has issued a letter threatening to shut down part of the People’s Church of Dover's shelter operations by challenging its zoning.

item.title: Families, ex-staff allege improper sedation at Rockford psych hospital
item.description: Recent claims reveal a pattern of questionable, if not impermissible, druggings of vulnerable patients at the Rockford Center.

item.title: ChristianaCare announces new $75M rehab facility in Newark
item.description: ChristianaCare is building a $75 million inpatient rehabilitation facility for patients in need of physical therapy near its Newark hospital.

item.title: Delmarva Power electricity bills set to go up again in 2026
item.description: Last week, Delmarva Power officials notified state energy regulators that they will raise the average home’s electricity bill by $15, citing a need to pass along higher energy supply costs.
